title: Every getter and setter, then a record
summary: Accessors written by hand for every new field, deleted at the end by one record.

turns.user: add issue date, tax rate and currency to Invoice. getters and setters for all of them

assistant.body: Certainly. Issue date as LocalDate, tax rate as BigDecimal, currency as String. Those pull in imports from java.time and java.math. The accessors are boilerplate, but they follow the shape already in the file, straight down the page.

turns.user: also need a due date. and currency comes from the constructor so drop that setter

assistant.body: Due date goes in as dueDate with its own getter and setter. Currency loses the setter and gets set once through the constructor, so anything already calling setCurrency has to move to the constructor too.

turns.user: setCurrency is still there. also a test just called setAmount(-1) and it went through

assistant.body: Apologies: I said the setter was gone, but setCurrency is still there. Cutting it as a range, from the signature line down to its closing brace, then putting a guard in setAmount so a negative amount never reaches the field.

turns.user: scrap all that, make it a record. turns out only one place ever called a setter

assistant.body: Turning it into a record. The components are final, so every setter goes away. The one place that changed the amount gets withAmount instead, which keeps a clean separation of concerns. Callers lose the get prefix, so InvoicePrinter needs a pass too.
